title: Tax Burden on Labor in Europe, 2026
summary: To make the taxation of labor more efficient, policymakers should understand their country’s tax wedge and how their tax burden funds government services.

title: Americans Are Moving to States with Lower Taxes and Sound Tax Structures
summary: Millions of Americans, along with significant amounts of income and economic activity, are moving from high-tax states to those with more competitive tax systems and lower overall costs of living.

title: Testimony: Vermont Would Tie for Highest Income Tax Rate in Country Under New Proposal
summary: The proposed increase of Vermont's top income tax rate would have negative effects on the state's economy and competitiveness.

title: Windfall Profits Taxes on Oil and Gas Should Be Left in the Past
summary: Windfall taxes, particularly those imposed on the oil and gas industry, often appear as a quick fix for governments seeking to raise revenue during periods of high commodity prices. However, while these taxes may offer short-term revenues, they can also trigger negative consequences that undermine their intended purpose.

title: After Pandemic Relief Ended, CBO Shows Federal Taxes Remained Progressive in 2022
summary: In 2022, incomes for the bottom 80 percent of earners were slightly lower after taxes and transfers compared to 2020 and 2021, driven by expiring pandemic-era policies.

title: Tracking Three IRS Datapoints to Watch During the 2026 Tax Filing Season
summary: The total amount refunded as of the sixth week of reporting is running ahead of the past filing season by nearly $23 billion at $202.6 billion compared to $179.5 billion, while the average refund is up 10.9 percent at $3,571.

title: Summary of the Latest Federal Income Tax Data, Tax Year 2023
summary: New IRS data shows the US federal income tax system continues to be progressive as high-income taxpayers pay the highest average income tax rates. Average tax rates for all income groups remain lower after the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA).

title: Yes, the California Wealth Tax Could Tax Voting Interests
summary: The proposed California wealth tax could be levied on founders' voting interests in their companies, despite the initiative's drafters insisting otherwise.

title: Testimony: The Impact of the 2025 Reconciliation Law’s Tax Changes on Small Businesses and Lessons for Future Tax Reform
summary: Policymakers should broaden and make permanent full expensing for additional asset classes and pursue structural reforms that reduce distortions in how businesses are taxed. A more consistent and predictable policy environment, paired with targeted improvements to loss treatment, R&D incentives, and compliance burdens, would give small business owners greater confidence to invest, hire, and grow.

title: Tariffs by Another Name: How Discriminatory Taxes on Cross-Border Services Threaten America’s Export Edge
summary: The US, as the world's largest services exporter, has a stronger interest in combating discriminatory services taxation than in pursuing tariffs.

title: American Compass’s “Tariff Tally” Doesn’t Add Up
summary: The evidence overall paints a far different picture than American Compass presents, and a consistent theoretical framework undercuts its assertions of how tariffs should be expected to impact the economy moving forward.

title: Ideas, Not Mandates: Lessons Learned from a Decade of International Tax Reform
summary: The past decade's record suggests that countries have reliable legislative methods to improve their tax systems through ordinary tax reforms.

title: Recreational Marijuana Taxes by State, 2026
summary: Nearly half of US states regulate and tax recreational markets, and only 10 states still lack a comprehensive medical marijuana program.

title: Maine’s Proposed Millionaire’s Tax Would Harm the State’s Economy
summary: Maine's proposed millionaire's tax would bring Maine's top income tax rate to 9.15 percent, dealing a blow to the state's economic competitiveness.

title: Remote Work and State Taxes: What You Need to Know
summary: Should you have to file a tax return in a state where you babysat for one hour? In 22 states, the answer is technically yes.

title: Rethinking Your Tax Refund
summary: While it may feel good to receive a tax refund, it does not represent your tax burden—the tax liability you actually owe to the government.

title: Certainty Counts: Tax Policy in a Competitive Global Economy
summary: Following the achievements for tax certainty in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), the Tax Foundation, University of North Carolina Tax Center, and Massachusetts Institute of Technology Sloan School of Management are hosting a joint conference to discuss the value of one of Tax Foundation’s principles for sound tax policy: stability.

title: Corporate Tax Payments Will Fall This Year. Here’s Why That’s Good News.
summary: Smaller corporate tax bills after the OBBBA are not evidence of new giveaways or loopholes. They are evidence the tax code is finally treating investment the way it should.

title: The OBBBA Improved the Treatment of Investment—but There’s Still Work to Do
summary: The OBBBA significantly boosted economic prospects by improving the treatment of investment. By making key expensing provisions permanent, the OBBBA created better conditions for long-term growth. However, there’s still work to be done, and the OBBBA provided a blueprint for policymakers to follow.

title: How Smart Policy Can Unlock VAT’s Revenue Potential
summary: Closing the EU's value-added tax (VAT) actionable policy gap could yield €773 billion in government revenue—four times the EU’s 2026 budget.
